verses.text: Then Jacob continued on his journey and came to the land of the eastern peoples.
There he saw a well in the open country, with three flocks of sheep lying beside it, because the flocks were given water from that well. The stone over the mouth of the well was large.

When all the flocks were gathered there, the shepherds would roll the stone away from the mouth of the well and give water to the sheep. Then they would put the stone back in its place over the mouth of the well.
Jacob asked the shepherds, "My friends, where are you from?" "We are from Haran," they replied.
He said to them, "Do you know Laban, Nahor's grandson?" "Yes, we know him," they answered.
Then Jacob asked them, "Is he well?" "Yes, he is well," they said. "And here comes his daughter Rachel with the sheep."
"Look," he said, "it is still the middle of the day. It is not time for the flocks to be gathered. Give the sheep water and take them back to the fields."
"We cannot," they replied, "until all the flocks are gathered and the stone has been rolled away from the mouth of the well. Then we will give the sheep water."
While he was still talking with them, Rachel came with her father's sheep, because she was a shepherd.
When Jacob saw Rachel, the daughter of his uncle Laban, with Laban's sheep, he went over and rolled the stone away from the mouth of the well and gave water to his uncle's sheep.
Then Jacob kissed Rachel and began to weep loudly.
He told Rachel that he was a relative of her father, the son of Rebekah. So she ran and told her father.
As soon as Laban heard the news about Jacob, his sister's son, he hurried to meet him. He hugged him and kissed him and brought him to his home. There Jacob told him all that had happened.
Then Laban said to him, "You really are my own flesh and blood." Jacob stayed with him for a whole month.
Then Laban said to him, "Just because you are my relative, you should not work for me for nothing. Tell me what your pay should be."
Now Laban had two daughters. The name of the older one was Leah, and the name of the younger one was Rachel.
Leah had gentle eyes, but Rachel had a lovely figure and was beautiful.
Jacob was in love with Rachel. So he said, "I will work for you for seven years in return for your younger daughter Rachel."
Laban said, "It is better that I give her to you than to some other man. Stay here with me."
So Jacob worked for seven years to get Rachel, but they seemed like only a few days to him because he loved her so much.
Then Jacob said to Laban, "Give me my wife. My time is finished, and I want to sleep with her."
So Laban brought together all the people of the place and gave a feast.
But when evening came, he took his daughter Leah and brought her to Jacob, and Jacob slept with her.
Laban gave his slave woman Zilpah to his daughter Leah as her servant.
When morning came, there was Leah! So Jacob said to Laban, "What have you done to me? I worked for you to get Rachel, did I not? Why have you tricked me?"
Laban replied, "It is not our custom here to give the younger daughter in marriage before the older one.
Finish this daughter's wedding week. Then we will give you the younger one too, in return for another seven years of work."
And Jacob did so. He finished the week with Leah, and then Laban gave him his daughter Rachel to be his wife.
Laban gave his slave woman Bilhah to his daughter Rachel as her servant.
Jacob slept with Rachel too, and he loved Rachel more than Leah. And he worked for Laban for another seven years.
When the LORD saw that Leah was not loved, he made it possible for her to have children, but Rachel could not have children.
Leah became pregnant and gave birth to a son. She named him Reuben, because she said, "The LORD has seen my trouble. Surely my husband will love me now."
She became pregnant again and gave birth to a son. She said, "Because the LORD heard that I am not loved, he has given me this son too." So she named him Simeon, which sounds like "heard".

Again she became pregnant and gave birth to a son. She said, "Now at last my husband will become attached to me, because I have given him three sons." So he was named Levi, which sounds like "attached".
She became pregnant once more and gave birth to a son. She said, "This time I will praise the LORD." So she named him Judah, which sounds like "praise". Then she stopped having children for a while.
